issues.legal_issue: The absence of a statutory appeal does not enlarge the High Court’s supervisory jurisdiction or permit it to reappreciate evidence as an appellate court.
material_facts: The challenged order was made by an inferior authority in a compulsory-purchase proceeding, and the statute provided no appeal against that order.
The High Court set the order aside after reassessing the valuation evidence and substituting its own conclusion for that of the authority.
issues.conclusion: The absence of an appeal did not enlarge the High Court’s supervisory power, and the High Court could not act as an appellate court by reappreciating the evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226 of the Constitution, supervisory review may interfere with a tribunal’s finding if it failed to consider relevant material, considered irrelevant or extraneous material, relied on no evidence, or reached a conclusion no reasonable person could reach on the evidence. The availability of a statutory appeal does not alter those limits. The Court relied on C.B. Gautam v. Union of India, which addressed the safeguards and conditions for compulsory purchase under Chapter XX-C, and discussed Kailash Suneja v. Appropriate Authority as confirming that sufficiency or adequacy of material is not open to judicial review and that relevant and extraneous material may be examined.

predicates.judicial_review_of_tribunal: A party asks a court exercising supervisory jurisdiction to review a decision made by an inferior tribunal.
predicates.no_statutory_appeal: The governing statutory scheme provides no appeal from the tribunal’s decision.

issues.definition: When a court reviews a tribunal’s decision and no statutory appeal is available, its review remains supervisory rather than appellate.

issues.legal_issue: A compulsory-purchase order is sustainable when the authority establishes significant undervaluation using relevant comparable sales, follows the required procedure, and the parties do not rebut the resulting presumption of tax evasion.
material_facts: The authority considered contemporaneous sale transactions in the same locality involving land with the same potentiality and concluded that the fair market rate was substantially higher than the rate in the agreement.
The authority found that the apparent consideration was lower than fair market value by more than fifteen percent.
The parties received an opportunity to be heard, and the authority recorded reasons for its valuation and purchase decision.
The transferor’s explanation that an urgent need for medical expenses led to the lower sale price was considered and rejected; no other positive ground rebutting the presumption was advanced.
issues.conclusion: The authority considered relevant material, discharged the burden of establishing significant undervaluation, and was justified in drawing an unrebutted presumption that the undervaluation was intended to evade tax. The High Court exceeded its jurisdiction by substituting its own assessment, so the compulsory-purchase order was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Chapter XX-C of the Income Tax Act, including Section 269-UD, compulsory purchase may be ordered where the apparent consideration is lower than fair market value by fifteen percent or more and the statutory preconditions are satisfied. Under C.B. Gautam v. Union of India, significant undervaluation may support a rebuttable presumption of an attempt to evade tax. The authority must give an opportunity to be heard and record reasons. Judicial review remains subject to the limited supervisory grounds described by the Court.

rule.if: compulsory_purchase_proceeding and comparable_local_sales and significant_undervaluation and fair_hearing_and_reasons and no_rebuttal_of_tax_evasion_presumption

predicates.compulsory_purchase_proceeding: The matter concerns an authority’s decision to purchase property compulsorily under a statutory scheme.
predicates.comparable_local_sales: The authority relied on contemporaneous sales in the same locality involving property with comparable potentiality.
predicates.significant_undervaluation: The authority found that the agreed consideration was substantially below the property’s fair market value.
predicates.fair_hearing_and_reasons: The authority gave the affected parties an opportunity to be heard and recorded reasons for its decision.
predicates.no_rebuttal_of_tax_evasion_presumption: The parties did not establish a persuasive ground rebutting the presumption that the significant undervaluation was intended to evade tax.

issues.definition: A compulsory-purchase order is sustainable when the proceeding involves comparable local sales, significant undervaluation, a fair hearing with reasons, and no successful rebuttal of the resulting presumption.

issues.legal_issue: The amount held on deposit together with the interest it has accrued may be directed to be paid to the affected parties when a compulsory-purchase order is upheld and the circumstances warrant that payment.
material_facts: The compulsory-purchase order was upheld, and the purchase money was held in deposit.
The deposited money had accrued interest.
The Court considered the circumstances and directed payment of the entire deposited amount together with the interest accrued on it.
issues.conclusion: The entire amount held in deposit, together with the interest accrued on it, was directed to be paid to the respondents.
issues.legal_principle: Whether interest is payable when a sale cannot be completed because of a compulsory-purchase order depends on the facts and circumstances of the case. Rajalakshmi Narayanan (Mrs.) v. Margaret Kathleen Gandhi (Mrs.) & Ors. states that interest may be appropriate where the owner has not obstructed the purchase or completion of the sale, cannot obtain the purchase price because of the order and a stay, and equity so requires. In this case, the Court directed payment of the deposited amount and accrued interest after considering the circumstances.

rule.if: compulsory_purchase_case and purchase_order_upheld and purchase_money_held_on_deposit and deposit_earned_interest

predicates.compulsory_purchase_case: The dispute concerns a statutory compulsory purchase of property agreed to be sold.
predicates.purchase_order_upheld: The court ultimately upholds the compulsory-purchase order.
predicates.purchase_money_held_on_deposit: The purchase money is held in deposit rather than having been paid out.
predicates.deposit_earned_interest: The money held in deposit has accrued interest.

issues.definition: When a compulsory-purchase order is upheld and the purchase money is held in an interest-bearing deposit, the deposited amount and its accrued interest may be directed to the affected parties.
